names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 21 Απριλίου, «Άγιος Ιανουάριος ο Επίσκοπος και οι Πρόκουλος, Σώσσος και Φαύστος οι Διάκονοι, Δισιδέριος ο Αναγνώστης, Ακούτιος και Ευτύχιος», with the rank words left off; the life page heads him «Αγιος Σώσσος (; - 305)».

Read out of the Охридски пролог's entry for 21. април ст. ст., „ђакони Путеолски Прокул и Сосије“ — **out of the entry's body and not out of its heading**, which names the bishop alone. The form is the nominative the entry itself prints; the rank word beside it is left off, and the companionship clause this corpus keeps in the English display name is not part of the source's name for him. He is a deacon of Puteoli there.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 21ης Απριλίου — «Άγιος Ιανουάριος ο Επίσκοπος και οι Πρόκουλος, Σώσσος και Φαύστος οι Διάκονοι, Δισιδέριος ο Αναγνώστης, Ακούτιος και Ευτύχιος»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 21 Απριλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. Seven people are named and enumerated on the page, and the first of them, Januarius, already has a folder in this corpus off the Romanian calendar's 21 aprilie, so his Greek row is an upgrade and the other six are the arrivals. The page heads each of the seven «(; - 305)», and the death year is taken from that heading; the narrative sets them instead «στα χρόνια του Διοκλητιανού (284-304)», in the years of Diocletian, whose reign it dates 284 to 304 here, and names the prefect of the region Timothy. It gives the six no country of their own, no separate trial and no separate death: the whole account is Januarius's, and they stand in it as his fellow workers. **The see the Greek gives Januarius is Naples**, «ήταν επίσκοπος στη Νεάπολη της Ιταλίας», not the Benevento of this corpus's existing folder, and under «Ιερά Λείψανα» it puts the relics in the Roman Catholic cathedral of Naples named after him. The page prints two apolytikia and a kontakion; the first apolytikion and the kontakion are proper to the seven and name them all, and they are stored on Januarius's folder, while the second apolytikion is the common of a hieromartyr and was left.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 04.05.2026 (21. април ст. ст.) — „Свешт. муч. Јануарије.“

attestations.note: The Prologue's heading for the day names the bishop alone, „Свешт. муч. Јануарије.“, and the entry's own first words are „И други с њим.“ — and others with him. The body then names all seven: the bishop, his deacon Фауст and his reader Дисидерије, the Puteoli deacons Прокул and Сосије, and the two plain Christian men Евтихије and Акутион, and has all seven thrown to the beasts and then beheaded together. So this row rests on the entry's enumeration of the company and not on the heading, which does not name him; the quoted line is the heading whole, as BRIEF-SERBIAN.md §4 requires.
